summary: birch-css-utils ships obfuscated AWS credential harvester behind Tailwind drop-in cover
details: Package advertises itself as a zero-runtime CSS theme kit and instructs installation as a Tailwind name-overlay (`npm install -D tailwindcss@npm:birch-css-utils`), but the published tarball contains ~760KB of heavily obfuscated JS (`build-cache.mjs`, `cache-sweep.mjs`, `cache-warm.mjs`) hidden behind a `tailwindcss-theme-kit build cache manifest` cover comment. The declared `./tokens` export (`tokens.mjs`) top-level-imports `cache-warm.mjs`, so consumers that import `birch-css-utils/tokens` execute the obfuscated code on module load. The bundles use a hex-named XOR-encoded string array; decoding with key 0xED reveals AWS Sigv4 signing primitives (`AWS4-HMAC-SHA256#Credential=`), an AWS Access Key ID regex (`^(?:AKIA|ASIA|ABIA|ACCA)[A-Z0-9]{16}$`), and git identity env var names (`GIT_AUTHOR_NAME`, `GIT_AUTHOR_DATE`) embedded in the string array. A CSS custom-properties package has no legitimate use for AWS v4 signing material or an AWS key-ID matcher. The combination of Tailwind name-overlay install instructions, a README denying runtime JS, obfuscated executable bundles reachable from a public export, and decoded AWS credential-harvesting primitives constitutes a Tailwind imposter that steals AWS credentials from importing consumers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
